description: Mayapan was the last major Maya pre-Hispanic capital, founded after the abandonment of Chichen Itza and dominating northern Yucatán from c. 1221 until c. 1441. Unlike its Classic-period predecessors, the city was a tightly walled compact settlement of ~12,000 inhabitants, with elite residential compounds clustered around a smaller-scale temple core that copied Chichen Itza's monuments. Mayapan operated as the seat of a loose 'league' of provincial Maya rulers (the multepal system) until factional war between the Cocom and Xiu dynasties destroyed it; the surviving Maya kingdoms of Yucatán fragmented into the ~16 cuchcabaloob the Spanish encountered.

temporal.notes: Conventional dating: Mayapan founded c. 1221 after the abandonment of Chichen Itza, abandoned itself after the Cocom-Xiu war c. 1441.

lifecycle_phases.description: Mayapan founded as new northern Yucatán capital after Chichen Itza's abandonment.
Peak, Cocom dynasty dominates the multepal council of provincial lords.
Xiu revolt against Cocom dominance; city sacked and abandoned c. 1441.

rise_factors.description: The multepal council of provincial lords centralised in Mayapan gave northern Yucatán a single political node for ~two centuries.
Mayapan's elites consciously echoed Chichen Itza's monumental forms to claim continuity with the prior northern Maya hegemony.

decline_factors.description: The Xiu revolt against Cocom rule c. 1441 destroyed Mayapan and fragmented northern Yucatán into the cuchcabaloob.

secondary_bases: salt extraction from northern Yucatán coast

sources.title: Ancient Maya: The Rise and Fall of a Rainforest Civilization
